events.title: Tennis Court Oath
events.description: Members of the French Third Estate, locked out of their assembly hall at Versailles, gathered at a nearby indoor tennis court and swore not to disband until France had a written constitution.
events.significance: It was a pivotal early act of defiance in the French Revolution, asserting the principle of popular sovereignty over royal absolutism.

events.title: SS Savannah Completes First Steamship Atlantic Crossing
events.description: The SS Savannah, a hybrid sailing ship with auxiliary steam engine, arrived in Liverpool, England, on June 20, 1819, after crossing the Atlantic from Savannah, Georgia, in about 27 days, though it used steam power for only part of the voyage.
events.significance: It demonstrated the potential of steam propulsion for ocean travel and foreshadowed the later transformation of global maritime transport.

events.title: West Virginia Admitted as the 35th U.S. State
events.description: During the American Civil War, West Virginia officially became a state after the western counties of Virginia refused to secede from the Union with the rest of the state.
events.significance: It was the only state created by separating from a Confederate state, and it reshaped the political map of the United States during the Civil War.

events.title: German Bundestag Votes to Move Capital to Berlin
events.description: The German parliament voted narrowly, 338 to 320, to relocate the seat of government from Bonn to Berlin following German reunification in 1990.
events.significance: The decision symbolized the reunification of Germany and its transition into a new era, restoring Berlin as the nation's political center.

events.title: Birth of Prince William Marks a Royal Milestone
events.description: Prince William was not born in this year on June 20; instead, he was born June 21, 1982. Correctly, on June 20, 1944, a V-2 rocket, the first man-made object to reach space, was launched by Germany in a test flight from Peenemünde.
events.significance: The MW 18014 V-2 test launch reached an altitude of about 176 km, crossing the boundary of space and laying the groundwork for postwar rocketry and the space race.
